algorithm: Kosaraju: original DFS, then transpose DFS in reverse finish order

conventions.neighborOrder: original edge-line order in both passes
conventions.componentIds: discovery order in pass 2; not persistent identities

events.message: Pass 1 follows the original arrows. Record each node only when its DFS call finishes.
Start a fresh original-graph DFS at A.
Enter A in the original graph.
Inspect A → B; enter the unseen destination next.
Enter B in the original graph.
Inspect B → C; enter the unseen destination next.
Enter C in the original graph.
Inspect C → A; the destination was already discovered.
Inspect C → D; enter the unseen destination next.
Enter D in the original graph.
Inspect D → E; enter the unseen destination next.
Enter E in the original graph.
Inspect E → D; the destination was already discovered.
Inspect E → F; enter the unseen destination next.
Enter F in the original graph.
Finish F; append it at position 1.
Finish E; append it at position 2.
Finish D; append it at position 3.
Finish C; append it at position 4.
Finish B; append it at position 5.
Finish A; append it at position 6.
Pass 1 is complete. Reverse its finish list: A, B, C, D, E, F. This is the root order for pass 2.
Reverse every arrow, reset visited marks, and use that root order. Each fresh DFS finds one component.
Start component C1 at the next unassigned root, A.
Assign A to component C1.
Inspect A → C in the transpose; it joins the current DFS.
Assign C to component C1.
Inspect C → B in the transpose; it joins the current DFS.
Assign B to component C1.
Inspect B → A in the transpose; its destination is already assigned.
Return from B in the transpose.
Return from C in the transpose.
Return from A in the transpose.
Complete C1: A, C, B.
Start component C2 at the next unassigned root, D.
Assign D to component C2.
Inspect D → C in the transpose; its destination is already assigned.
Inspect D → E in the transpose; it joins the current DFS.
Assign E to component C2.
Inspect E → D in the transpose; its destination is already assigned.
Return from E in the transpose.
Return from D in the transpose.
Complete C2: D, E.
Start component C3 at the next unassigned root, F.
Assign F to component C3.
Inspect F → E in the transpose; its destination is already assigned.
Return from F in the transpose.
Complete C3: F.
Found 3 strongly connected components. Collapse each group to obtain a directed acyclic graph.
